clue.text: Guides the cattle

definitions.meaning: to guide something is to direct its course, a verb in the third person
young castrated bulls raised for beef, plural

explanation.surface: A drover's handbook entry: the people who direct the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct a course, and bullocks raised for beef are called by the same word.

clue.text: Suggested that the little devil told fibs!

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
lied means told untruths

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a mischievous child has been lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hinted at without being stated outright is suggested.

clue.text: Formulate surface + pitch + variable quantity of the spheres

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface
tar is black pitch
y is a standard algebraic symbol for an unknown variable

explanation.surface: An equation built from a surface, a pitch and a variable, as if astronomy were algebra.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written as a sum; 'Formulate' simply invites you to add the pieces up.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets were once carried on celestial spheres, so anything relating to those bodies is planetary.

clue.text: Air filter

definitions.meaning: to pass liquid through a sieve, a verb

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction for cleaning the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or a tune, and to strain liquid is to sieve it.

clue.text: Meditating on sinful, gullible fool

annotationWithheld.why: Meditating on sinful, gullible fool: the parse is MUG round SIN, but 'sinful' gives SIN and its '-ful' suffix is the only container signal, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Rodents who dig trenches around the French river

indicators.note: the word for trenches is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: moats are defensive trenches around a castle
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Burrowing animals tunnel beneath the defences around a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: Mole rats are burrowing African rodents that spend their lives tunnelling underground.

clue.text: Play in a peculiar way at first

indicators.note: tells you the word for way comes before the word for peculiar

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A musician performs in an odd manner right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as 'odd' is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to play a guitar or similar instrument by sweeping across the strings.

clue.text: Nearly stupefied, one has sense of relating to deity

indicators.note: the word for stupefied loses its final letter, coming nearly but not quite complete

parts.note: numb means stunned or stupefied
I is the Roman numeral for one
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Someone dazed still has a feeling of a divine presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of NUMB to leave NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Numinous describes the awe-inspiring sense of a divine or spiritual presence.

clue.text: A pattern office worker is dead-set on

indicators.note: places the word for office worker on top of the word for dead, so it comes first

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
late means deceased, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A clerk is utterly determined to follow a set design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead-set on' reads as one phrase meaning determined; split it to get 'dead' and the placing signal 'set on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a shaped guide or model used as a pattern for copying.

clue.text: Danger signals when a mural's demolished

indicators.note: a demolished wall's letters are knocked about and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters of mural plus S, the 's counting here

explanation.surface: Warnings sound as a wall painting is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarums is an archaic spelling of alarms, calls to arms or warnings of danger.

clue.text: Terry has 11/4 yards to measure for printer

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of one and a quarter yards (45 inches)
an en is a printer's unit of width

explanation.surface: An actor needs cloth measured out for a print job.
explanation.walkthrough: '11/4' is one and a quarter, the length of an ell; Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian stage star Terry had the given name Ellen, so her surname leads to her first name.

clue.text: Increase in building material with right admixture

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an admixture is something mixed into another substance, so one letter goes into the material

parts.note: cement is a building material

explanation.surface: A rise in construction materials owing to an added ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a step up or addition in amount, a growth.

clue.text: First national guard outfit that is not a ruling body

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: A national guard's first unit turns out not to be the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-governmental organisation is a body independent of the state, a charity or campaign group.

clue.text: Coming down coldly on errant gent's lie

indicators.note: errant means straying or wandering, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: the letters of gent plus S

explanation.surface: A wandering gentleman's falsehood falls on someone frostily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is icy rain, so weather that is sleeting is falling cold and half-frozen.

clue.text: Where Paul was born, in a boat, with stars out all around

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the boat letter on every side
out means awry or wrong, so the letters of stars are disordered

parts.note: a U-boat was a German submarine, so the boat gives U

explanation.surface: A saint's birthplace pictured as sitting in a boat under a ring of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of STARS (TARSS) goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Paul was born in the city of Tarsus in what is now southern Turkey.

clue.text: A range of hills or mountains in Italy

parts.note: the Pennines are a range of hills running down northern England

explanation.surface: A geography question asking for a range of hills or mountains in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the hill chain known as the backbone of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running down the length of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Permit and distribute after-dinner drink

parts.note: to pass something round is to distribute it
port is a fortified wine traditionally served after dinner

explanation.surface: A host allows and hands round a glass of something after the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document permitting its holder to travel abroad.

clue.text: Adam's was turned to Eve

parts.note: in Genesis God takes a bone from Adam's side and forms the first woman from it; 'turned to' reads like 'turned towards'

explanation.surface: Adam's attention shifted towards Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says the first woman was fashioned from a bone taken from the first man's side.

clue.text: Pacific line car I wrecked

indicators.note: a wrecked car is smashed up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A calm stretch of road where I crashed the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenical means promoting peace, from the Greek for peace, so it means peaceable.

clue.text: When quiet, snake appears

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: A snake shows up once things go silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous Egyptian cobra or viper.

clue.text: Trading place for a year, being a self-sacrificing type

parts.note: a mart is a market
yr is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a market stall for twelve months as a selfless gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr suffers or dies for a cause, giving up their own interest for others.

clue.text: In robins, it's a band around the middle

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue word robins, between its outer letters

explanation.surface: A bird spotter notes that robins have a stripe across the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn round the waist with a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Dogged fighter?

parts.note: read 'dogged' as a canine one and a fighter as a soldier: a feisty breed of dog, and in British slang a part-time Territorial Army soldier

explanation.surface: A tenacious combatant who never gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tenacious breed of dog and a member of the Territorial Army.

clue.text: If wet, they'll spoil your fun

definitions.text: If wet, they'll spoil your fun

parts.words: If wet, they'll spoil your fun
parts.note: soaked bedding is miserable, but the phrase with 'wet' in front names killjoys

explanation.surface: A warning that rain will ruin your day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a killjoy who dampens everyone's enjoyment.

clue.text: A poet who's nearly having fun

indicators.note: the word for having fun stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: larking means playing about, having fun

explanation.surface: A versifier who is almost fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin wrote The Whitsun Weddings and was one of England's best-known modern poets.

clue.text: Carol, once in, is sorting the men from the girls!

definitions.text: sorting the men from the girls

indicators.note: the word for once goes inside the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
ex means former, what something once was

explanation.surface: A carol singer who was once a member is now separating boys and girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexing animals means determining whether each is male or female.

clue.text: Scold angrily when Italian wine is given round — a bloomer

indicators.note: the wine is wrapped round the word for scolding, enclosing it

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy
to rant is to rail at someone furiously

explanation.surface: Someone rails furiously when handed Italian wine, which turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is something that blooms, a flower, and astrantia is the garden flower masterwort.

clue.text: Latin-American city needs a time to get in proportion

indicators.note: these letters must get inside the city's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, commonly shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A South American city needs time to get things in perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, their proportion.

clue.text: Glasgow park where they have a ball!

definitions.text: Glasgow park where they have a ball!

parts.words: Glasgow park where they have a ball!
parts.note: having a ball means a great time, but here a football is literally in play at a Glasgow ground

explanation.surface: A Scottish park where everyone enjoys themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibrox Park is the stadium of Rangers football club in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibrox is the Glasgow stadium where Rangers play football.

clue.text: Lock mice in or trap first

indicators.note: the word mice has the following letters put in it
only the opening letter of trap is taken

explanation.surface: Use a lock, or else set a mousetrap first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is shorthand: a mortice is the slot cut into a door, and a mortice lock is fitted into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortice lock is set into a slot cut in the door, and the lock is called by that name alone.

clue.text: Anais has the energy to take on young person's number

parts.note: Anais Nin was a French-born American diarist and novelist
E is the physics symbol for energy
a teen is a teenager, a young person

explanation.surface: A writer finds the stamina to handle a youngster's phone number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteen is a whole number, one more than eighteen.

clue.text: Saunter via street to bridge, perhaps

parts.note: a bridge roll is a small soft finger-shaped bread roll, so bridge is an example of a roll

explanation.surface: Ambling down the road to cross a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridge roll is a British party-food bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, as is a saunter.
